narrative.overview:
The morning brief's paper, read like an exchange. Every surface made for the Director and his managers — the 08:00 brief picture, the A4 report PDFs (`integrations/reports/templates/`) and the PULSE screen (`integrations/api/static/pulse.*`) — is near-black ink on a white page, divided by hairline rules, set in one sans with tabular figures. PULSE carries that paper onto a screen and borrows a trading terminal's grammar: a quote with its arrow, a pulse line over volume bars, a time-and-sales tape, a ranked board. Dark mode is the same paper on a graphite ground, not a second theme. The public customer pages (`/f` complaints in red, `/r` reviews in green), their QR cards and the `/db` viewer are outside this system and keep their own settled looks.

Density is a terminal's: many figures, very few words. Every user-facing word is Uzbek Cyrillic (business and product names stay as written: PULSE, Garmin, Primus, Londry), and the owner's standing order is to add no more text — numbers, arrows and lines carry the meaning. Colour is never decoration: green, amber and red mean good, late and needs-the-Director, and nothing else. Structure comes from rules and alignment; there are no shadows, no gradients and no tiles.

Rejected outright: the card-grid dashboard of equal tiles, rounded card soup, emoji.
keyCharacteristics: White paper (graphite in dark mode), near-black ink, three line weights.
Noto Sans 400 and 700 only; tabular, lining figures everywhere.
State colour only: green good, amber late, red for what needs the Director.
Drawn stroke icons and drawn ▲/▼ marks, never glyphs or emoji.
Flat: no shadows, no gradients; regions are ruled, never boxed.
Uzbek Cyrillic, as few words as possible.

rules.name: The Red-Is-for-the-Director Rule
rules.body: Red marks only what needs the Director: a bad change, an absence, a missed report, a complaint. Never emphasis, branding or a heading.

rules.name: The Good-Not-Sign Rule
rules.body: The drawn ▲/▼ shows the sign; the colour shows whether it is good. Complaints going up are a red ▲. Zero or unknown is Pencil Grey, never green.

rules.name: The One-Paper Rule
rules.body: Dark mode re-points the same tokens to graphite; on screen, no hue, token or component exists in only one mode. Charts read their colours from the CSS custom properties at paint time and repaint when the scheme changes.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every figure is tabular and lining (`tnum`, `lnum`), so tickers and columns hold still while values change. Thousands group with a space and decimals take a comma (ru-RU): 1,3 млрд.

rules.name: The Quiet Unit Rule
rules.body: A unit sits after its number at 13px 400 in Slate Ink (млрд, млн, минг, сўм, %), never at the figure's size or weight.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: 400 and 700 only; no italics, no second family. Hierarchy is size and weight.

rules.name: The Equal Phone Rule
rules.body: The phone is a first reader, not a fallback: every view works in one column at a 16px gutter with no horizontal page scroll, and every control there is at least 40px tall.

rules.name: The Flat Paper Rule
rules.body: Nothing casts a shadow and nothing fades. An element that must sit above the page gets an edge (1px Strong Rule) or inverts to ink.

rules.name: The Three Weights Rule
rules.body: 2px Press Ink under the top bar and a sheet's head (the masthead rule); 1px Strong Rule under a section head and around controls; 1px Hairline between rows, tickers and gridlines. No fourth weight.

dos: **Do** write every user-facing word in Uzbek Cyrillic; keep business and product names as written (PULSE, Garmin, Primus, Londry).
**Do** keep text to the minimum: a label is one or two words, and numbers, arrows and lines carry the rest.
**Do** show missing data as "—" in Pencil Grey, and step over a missing day in a line — never draw it as zero.
**Do** set every figure tabular and lining, with its unit at 13px 400 in Slate Ink.
**Do** bound regions with the three rule weights: 2px Press Ink for the masthead, 1px Strong Rule under a section head, 1px Hairline between rows.
**Do** draw icons as 24-unit strokes in `currentColor`, and draw ▲/▼ as filled triangles.
**Do** give every screen token a graphite value and read chart colours from the CSS custom properties, repainting when the colour scheme changes.
**Do** turn every animation and transition off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** build a grid of equal cards or boxed KPI tiles; tickers sit on hairlines.
**Don't** use shadows, gradients or blur; the chart's fill is one flat wash.
**Don't** use green, amber or red for decoration, branding, headings or emphasis.
**Don't** colour a delta by its sign alone: complaints rising are red, and flat or unknown is Pencil Grey.
**Don't** use emoji or font glyphs (⚠, ✓, ▲ characters) as icons.
**Don't** add a second typeface, a third weight or italics, or load fonts from a third-party host.
**Don't** box or round sections, the tape, the board or a sheet; a filled Ledger Band panel (6–8px corners) is only for a single callout inside a report.
**Don't** add explanatory captions, helper copy or tooltips of prose.
